title: Multifactorial intervention and rate of incident falls
description:
Intervention: multifactorial-interventions. Comparator: trial-comparator. Outcome: incident-fall-rate.

Multifactorial intervention versus contributing trial comparator arms: incidence rate ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.74 to 0.95), 20 trials, 22,115 participants, longest follow-up 6 to 28 months. Heterogeneity I-squared = 85.0% (supplied AHRQ abstract). This estimate applies to incident fall rate, not the number of people who fall.

Recommendation grade C: The USPSTF recommends individualizing whether to offer multifactorial interventions to community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older at increased fall risk, considering prior falls, comorbidities and patient preferences.

USPSTF assessed moderate certainty of a small net benefit for its recommendation. Routine provision to everyone is not the recommended decision.

Harms: Harms were sparsely reported; five trials with 4,199 participants reported generally rare, minor effects, often associated with exercise components.

Limitations: Trial components, baseline risks, implementation and adherence varied. Pooled results did not establish statistically significant reductions in people falling, injurious falls, fractures or mortality; this is not proof of no effect.
